items.problem: The role of the person operating the ticket checker moves from B to A: turn 2 establishes B is the one on the official checker waiting for it to load, but turn 4 has B telling A to refresh it and turn 5 has A reading the result off the checker.

The job-seeker role moves from B to A: turns 2 and 4 establish B as the interviewee who is reading the employer's message, but turn 5 has A speaking as that person ("asking me to schedule another interview").

Turns 1–2 establish B as the applicant (B interviewed, B's references were requested), but turn 4 has B telling A that A has the new email from the employer, and turn 5 has A opening and reading A's own offer details — the job-seeker role moves from B to A.

The role of the person with access to the account moves from B to A: turns 1–4 establish B as the one checking, with B's account, B's app, and B's phone alert, while A is the one asking and speculating without information. Turn 5 then has A announcing the result of that check — knowledge only B could have from the app B just opened.

The role of the person with the bag and the list moves from B to A: turns 2 and 4 establish B as the one checking the bag against the list and searching the side pocket, but turn 5 has A announcing the charger has been found and that everything on the list is packed — the search result and list knowledge that belonged to B.

The on-site observer role moves from B to A: turn 4 establishes that B is standing at the gym entrance looking at a notice on the door, but turn 5 has A reporting what that notice says, information only the person at the door could have.

The role of the person in contact with the restaurant moves from B to A: B is the one planning and receiving Marlowe's message in turn 4, but in turn 5 A is the one delivering the message's contents, knowledge only its recipient could have.

The soda-avoider role moves from B to A. Turn 2 establishes B as the one keeping off soda (bringing water so B doesn't buy any), but turn 5 has A delivering that person's reaction to the Dr. Pepper cooler in the first person — "I'm never going to stop drinking it."

Turns 1-3 establish A as the person adopting from the shelter — A got the update, A received the photo, A hasn't picked a name — but turn 5 has A telling B "You actually got one," moving the adopter role from A to B.

The gift-recipient role moves from B to A: turns 2–4 establish B as the one opening the presents and whose year-long wish list Mom tracked (A even says "things you'd mentioned"), but in turn 5 A speaks as that recipient, saying Mom got everything "I mentioned."
